Subject: MAP: Load test scheduling & capacity sizing

Marissa / team,

Thanks again for the demo this morning — really helpful to see Redwood's routing and caching features in action. As discussed, Samir and I put together a quick draft of the Mutual Action Plan items we want to validate before commit. The key milestone we're focused on this week is the load/performance test so we can size the Dedicated capacity and lock in pricing.

Quick recap of what we covered and what we need from Redwood:
- Objective: Traffic replay-based load test that simulates our peak trading hour (peak QPS and request size distribution) to validate latency and cost at scale.
- Target close date: 2026-07-29 (we're aiming to finalize capacity and PO by then).
- Load test window: prefer 2026-07-13 or 2026-07-14 (our ops team is available those mornings PST).
- Replay artifacts: we'll provide a captured replay (sample attached) + guidelines. Need confirmation of accepted format and max file size.
- Deliverables from Redwood: proposed Dedicated capacity sizing, expected RPS/QPS headroom, and one-hour latency P95 numbers under that sizing. Also a short runbook for test execution and rollback.

I've attached: MAP-FinLytics-v2.0.pdf (draft MAP), traffic-replay-guidelines.txt, and a small capture 'replay-capture-20260705.tar.gz' (redacted sample).

Action items for Redwood: please confirm your preferred replay ingestion format, confirm which of the proposed test dates works, and assign owners for the test day (primary contact + escalation). Also flag any dependencies we need to resolve (e.g., IP allowlists, VPC peering windows).

Thanks —
Olivia Chen

- Target milestone: "Load/Performance Validation"
  - Goal: Validate latency and throughput under replay of peak trading hour; produce capacity recommendation for Dedicated sizing and cost estimate.
  - Target complete: 2026-07-15 (this is a soft target so we can still hit your 07/29 close date).
  - Milestone owner (Redwood): Vivek Kulkarni (Solutions Engineering) — test orchestration, traffic ingestion, run execution.

  - Success criteria: P95 latency <= 350ms for 95% of requests under the proposed sizing OR documented tradeoffs + cost numbers.

Proposed test schedule (please confirm):
- Candidate 1: 2026-07-13 09:00-12:00 PDT (capture ingestion + full 1-hour replay at peak QPS)
- Candidate 2: 2026-07-14 09:00-12:00 PDT

Requests for Aditya (SRE): can you please propose the Dedicated capacity configuration (instance type / node count) for a replay that hits ~12k peak QPS and ~120 byte average payload? Also confirm any infra prep (network rules, expected warmup time, KV cache priming steps).

Requests for Vivek: can you take point on runbook and confirm Redwood primary/escalation contacts for the test day?

I'll hold the MAP doc as the mutual source of truth; Olivia, if the dates above look good we can lock one in and I'll create the HubSpot activity and DocuSign PO task once we've validated sizing.

Thanks —

Subject: Re: MAP: Load test scheduling & capacity sizing (internal)

Marissa / Vivek — quick tech validation from SRE side. Thanks for looping me in. Notes below that we'll share with Olivia once we confirm date: 

1) Replay format / ingestion- Preferred: RedW-CSV (timestamp, method, path, body-b64, headers-json) OR pcap + metadata JSON (start offset mapping). Max recommended single-file size: 20GB; for larger captures use segmented tar.gz pieces. The attached traffic-replay-guidelines.txt covers this.

2) Peak QPS / sizing estimate- You listed ~12k peak QPS with ~120 byte payload average. For that profile our initial estimate is: Dedicated pool = 3 x A100-80GB (or 2 x p4d) sized for sustained peak with 25% headroom for bursts. This assumes model variant is LLM-m-medium (quantized) — if you plan to use a larger model we should recalc. - Expected latency P95: ~250-380ms depending on batching policy and KV cache hit rate. We'll run a short warmup to prime KV cache before the full replay.

3) Prep / dependencies- Network: please share source IP ranges for FinLytics traffic replay ingestion and any VPC peering times.
- Warmup: allow 20-30 minutes before a full one-hour peak run for cache priming.
- Observability: we'll provide a runbook with Grafana links and where to watch token-level cost.

4) Availability- I'm available on 2026-07-13 morning and can be on-call during the test. Vivek, please confirm if you want me to own the capacity scaling knobs or if you will.

I'll convert this into a short technical appendix to the MAP and share with Olivia once we pick a date.

—Aditya
